en.units.intro: Find a unit by its name or id and read its stats in plain words. Here you rename it, change what it is made of or copy it into your mod; its numbers (price, armour, cooldown, rank) are changed under Balance, Quick changes. Every change is shown first; nothing is written until you press Write.
en.units.intro.tune: Find a unit by its name or id and read its stats in plain words, then change one of its numbers: price, armour, cooldown, rank needed or head start. Its name and what it is made of are changed under Units. Every change is shown first; nothing is written until you press Write.

en.units.pickone: Pick a unit in the search list first.
en.units.unlockF: Unlock: wait at the start = cooldown x game factor x (1 - head start) = {c} x {k} x (1 - {f}) = {w} s. After each buy: {c} x {k} = {a} s. The game factor comes from the game mode settings (most modes use the same one).
en.units.notBuyable: This unit has no price card, so it is not in the buy panel.
en.units.legend.price: Price: points paid in the buy panel. MP is manpower. SP is special points (the hero button). A mod can add its own points, such as DP. Prices in different points are never compared.
en.units.legend.rank: Rank needed: the player rank (level) from which the button opens. Whole numbers only.
en.units.legend.charge: Cooldown: seconds the button waits after a buy. Whole numbers only; 30.0 crashes the game.
en.units.legend.fore: Head start: 0 to 1. 1 means ready at the start, 0.5 means half the cooldown at the start.
en.units.legend.armor: Armour f/s/r/t: front, side, rear, top in mm, from the thickest part.
en.units.legend.gun: Main gun: range in map units (20 = 1 m), damage and penetration of the default shell.
en.units.legend.crew: Crew: soldiers that come with the unit.
en.units.legend.speed: Top speed: the MaxSpeed value of the unit file.
en.units.legend.bots: Bots: armies whose computer players buy it (from bot.data.lua).
en.units.ch.h.cost: Price in command points, for example 400.
en.units.ch.h.name: The name players see in the buy panel and on the unit.
en.units.ch.h.armor: Numbers in mm, as many as the part has now (front side rear top). Use _ to keep one.
en.units.ch.goh.h: Gates of Hell: a part takes mm for every side, then the sides that differ (40, front 90, top 20) or one side (front 90); every part takes a percent (120 = 20% thicker); top speed takes km/h. A file shared with other units is copied next to this one. The class entry takes another armour class of the same kind (tank_heavy_tier1); a repair entry takes seconds, 1 to 600; a keys entry takes the volume keys (caststeel 0.8, highhardness yes, able.holed 1), a key left out is removed; the hull entry takes steel or wood.
en.units.ch.h.charge: Seconds, whole number. 0 means no wait.

en.units.ad.botsOff: Bots will never buy the new unit.

en.units.by.seat: Sits with {n}: same button, cooldown group, tags, rank and cooldown.

en.units.info.CLONE_MODEL_REF: The copy uses the 3D model and textures of the unit you copied; they are not copied into the mod, so it looks the same.
en.units.info.CLONE_NO_ASSETS: The unit you copied has no own 3D model file to copy; the copy points at the same one.
en.units.info.ROSTER_LINE: A buy-panel card for the new unit is added next to the card of the unit you copied.
en.units.info.GEN_WRECK_AUTOCLONE: The wreck (what is left when it is destroyed) is copied too, so the new unit leaves a wreck.
en.units.info.GEN_XX_AUTOCLONE: The second wreck stage is copied too, so the wreck can burn out the same way.
en.units.info.GEN_ROSTER_REPLACES: The mod gets its own copy of the bot buy list; it replaces the game list, so other mods that change bot buying are covered by this one.
en.units.id.bad: The new id: lower-case letters, digits and _ only, start with a letter, 2 to 41 characters.
en.units.id.x: Do not end the id with _x: that ending is kept for wrecks.

en.units.ds.byAi: Read by the AI model {m}. The plan was checked against the game units before it was shown.

en.units.ds.shared: New files: unit definition, its own copy of the 3D model, gun, name and buy panel line. The shells are the ones of the starting unit. The model copy looks the same unless a turret was swapped.
en.units.ds.goh.gun: Gun words left out on Gates of Hell: only a card with its own vehicle copy, whose weapon is a cannon file of the game gun folder, can get a changed gun.
en.units.ds.goh.armor: Armour words left out on Gates of Hell: only a card with its own vehicle copy can take new armour, and that armour must be in the copy's own files (not two shared files deep).
en.units.ds.goh.speed: Speed words left out on Gates of Hell: only a card with its own vehicle copy can take a new top speed, and its chassis speed must be in the copy's own files.

en.units.ds.goh.price: Price left out: this Gates of Hell squad is built by a macro with no price of its own; the game adds up its members (GHGPL-10).
en.units.ds.goh.card: Gates of Hell: the new unit is a copy of the card (id, name, men, own price) in units/<period>/units_<army>.set; a vehicle that buys itself also gets its own copy of the unit files. Not tested in game.

en.units.sk.intro: The skin is the body and uniform a soldier wears. A texture variant swaps the pictures painted on a model for another set, for example winter or camouflage paint. Pick another one, press Preview, then Write. Only files in your mod folder are written.
en.units.sk.nowNone: The soldier file names no skin, so the game shows a bare skeleton.
en.units.sk.lost: The game data has no skin file named {s}. Pick a skin from the list.
en.units.sk.shared: {n} other soldiers wear this skin too. Changing this soldier does not change them.
en.units.sk.vehNoSkin: A vehicle wears no skin. Its texture variant can be changed below.
en.units.sk.find.ph: Type part of a skin name, an army or a soldier, for example ger officer
en.units.sk.empty: The game data has no skins.
en.units.sk.none: No skin matches. Try a shorter word.
en.units.sk.count: {n} skins under {g} headings. Click a heading to open it.
en.units.sk.useNo: Open a soldier whose skin can be changed first.
en.units.sk.texNoFiles: The files of this model have no texture variants, so there is nothing to pick.
en.units.sk.texLost: The file names the variant {v}, but the model has no texture files for it. The game drops it and shows the plain textures.
en.units.sk.texAfterSkin: Write the new skin first. Then pick its texture variant.
en.units.sk.texSoldier: A soldier takes the variant from the file of his skin. Other soldiers wear that file too, so it is left alone: this soldier gets a copy of the skin file with the variant you pick, placed in your mod.
en.units.sk.texAliases: The file also lists variants a map can ask for by name: {a}.
en.units.sk.texMap: In a multiplayer match the map sets a variant of its own (0, 1, 2 or d in the original maps). It replaces this one when the model has texture files of that name. This one shows on maps that name none, in single player and in the editor.
en.units.sk.texMapGoh: Gates of Hell: this was read from the game files and not tried in the game. The season of a map may still replace the variant.
en.units.sk.nochange: Pick another skin or another texture variant first.
en.units.sk.viewHint: This changes the picture only. Nothing is written.
en.units.sk.viewSkin: The picture shows the picked skin with the variant its file names.
en.units.sk.viewNeedMod: Pick your mod folder to see the textures in the picture.
en.units.sk.why.nobreed: This file is not a soldier file the game reads, so its skin cannot be changed here.
en.units.sk.why.many: The soldier file has more than one skin line. Leave one in the file first.
en.units.sk.why.inherited: This soldier file has no skin line of its own. It takes its lines from another file that other soldiers share, so the skin is not changed here.
en.units.sk.why.form: The skin line of the soldier file names no skin.
en.units.sk.why.goh: In Gates of Hell a soldier shows the look of the season of the map. A multiplayer map gives every unit it spawns the texMod line of its mode file (map/multi/<map>/<mode>.info, for example texMod winter); a soldier placed in a mission has a TexMod line of his own. He wears that look when his skin has files of that name (<mesh>#winter.ply, <texture>#winter.dds), else his plain look. Pick a variant in the picture to see it. Read from the game files, not tried in the game.
en.units.sk.gohAlways: To make this soldier wear a look on every map, pick it above (for example winter): he gets a copy of his skin file with a texmod line naming it, in your mod. A winter map shows winter anyway; on a map whose season his skin has no files for he keeps the picked look. The skins of the game never use this line: it comes from the game of AS64 and was not tried in Gates of Hell, so test it in the game.
en.units.sk.gohMaps: Seasons the multiplayer maps of the game give: {list}. A season his skin has no files for leaves him in his plain look.
en.units.sk.gohMapsN: {s} on {n} map modes of {m} maps (for example {ex})
en.units.sk.why.noskin: The soldier has no skin, so there is no texture variant to pick.
en.units.sk.why.nodef: The file of the skin was not found, so its texture variants cannot be read.
en.units.sk.why.list: The file sets its textures one by one. That form is not changed here.
en.units.sk.why.manyLines: The file has more than one texture variant line. Leave one in the file first.
en.units.sk.why.nomodel: The file does not name its model itself (a shared file does), so the texture variant line cannot be placed in it.

en.units.kit.veh.intro: A vehicle works the same way: its own box with shells, ammunition and other items is the grid, and its weapon slots are listed under it. Pick a vehicle above, or press Equipment beside a vehicle in the 3D view list.

en.units.kit.veh.already: The vehicle already carries {n}. Change its count below.

en.units.kit.veh.sharedNote: Some items come from a file that other vehicles use too. They are shown and can not be changed here.

en.units.kit.sl.cant: This slot is not changed here.
en.units.kit.sl.find: Search what goes into this slot
en.units.kit.sl.nothing: Nothing in the game goes into this slot.
